en: I'm sorry.
note: shared (Romy, Marlene, Lily); variants add the joining space where it follows another fragment on the same line, and a trailing space before #6264 in 247186

en: Would you mind choosing a different flower?
I don't mind, but...
How odd. It wasn't spoiled or anything.
Please, take this one instead.
Do come again.
Please come again, if you like.
Thank you for the other day.
The gerberas are really lovely today.
Then I think I'll take those.
A flower as radiant as you are.
Oh, how sweet of you,
Do you run this shop all by yourself, Romy?
Mother loved flowers. Father was a botanist.
I see. But you're a strong person.
You can still smile so brightly like that.
I cried a great deal when I lost my parents.
But I can't go on crying forever,
can I?
Please, give me your orders
note: thrall line; followed by six #180 dots

en: What is it? The shop isn't open yet.
I'm taking a rest right now, so
keep it down, would you.
You're a stubborn one. Come back when the shop's open.
What is it? The shop isn't open right now, so
don't you go barging in here.
You're a stubborn one too, aren't you?
Well, well.
What brings you here when the shop isn't even open?
There's nothing for you here, you know.
Welcome. This is the general store.
We've got all sorts of handy things.
Anything you're after?
Let's see
how about a handkerchief?
Ah, I'm afraid I'm all out of those.
I do have soap, though.
Why, you don't need a towel for your hands.
If they're washed clean, there's no problem at all.
note: #5557/#5558 rebuilt as two sentences (JP splits one sentence across the line)

en: We've got all sorts of handy things, so
take your time and have a good look.
Is there anything you're after?
Oh, back again, are you?
Welcome. Oh, it's you.
There's something I want to ask you.
Ever been in those shops on Market Street?
<I've been there>
note: menu choice, not in any used_in

en: <I've never been>
note: menu choice, not in any used_in

en: What?
You mean you've been there too?
Of course you haven't.
note: not in any used_in; presumably Anna's reply to <I've never been>, before #5571

en: Naturally, decent folk wouldn't know
a barbaric place like that.
Those market folk, see, don't have the money
or a license to open a shop, so they just
note: also follows #5625 (slice 070), which must read like #5573

en: sell their goods on the street as they please.
Honestly, they get in the way of my business,
and it's a real nuisance
Lately, this shop's sales haven't been
so good, you know.
And I'm sure it's all because of those
market people
Ooh, they make my blood boil.
Don't you go shopping
at that market of theirs.
They're a bunch of swindlers.
What a noisy old hag.
Where a customer shops is his own business.
Wh-
note: stammer; the scene continues in msg 222287 with #5589

en: Why, how rude
I'm only 38, I'll have you know.
Welcome. Oh, it's only you.
Back again,
to make more nasty remarks?
Is that any way
to talk to a customer?
Hmph. Let me tell you, I can't stand
sucking up to people.
Good grief. With a temper like that, you're
hardly cut out for serving customers.
note: #5600 (slice 070) follows on its own line as a full sentence
